source: Calculated by Publick from the Connecticut Office of Policy and Management's mill rates and the statewide Parcel and CAMA file

years.calculated: The average assessed value of 13,426 single-family homes in the state's 2024 parcel file, times the fiscal year 2025 mill rate. Connecticut assesses homes at 70% of market value. It's the bill before exemptions and credits.

The average assessed value of 13,416 single-family homes in the state's 2025 parcel file, times the fiscal year 2026 mill rate. Connecticut assesses homes at 70% of market value. It's the bill before exemptions and credits. Assessments are phased in over 4 years after the revaluation of October 2024, as on the tax bills: each home's value here is its assessment before the revaluation, from the state's 2024 parcel file, plus 25% of any increase (year 1 of 4). A decrease isn't phased in.

The average assessed value of 13,428 single-family homes in the state's 2026 parcel file, times the fiscal year 2027 mill rate. Connecticut assesses homes at 70% of market value. It's the bill before exemptions and credits. Assessments are phased in over 4 years after the revaluation of October 2024, as on the tax bills: each home's value here is its assessment before the revaluation, from the state's 2024 parcel file, plus 50% of any increase (year 2 of 4). A decrease isn't phased in.
